newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk petrochemical, oil workers to block shipments.
newsitem.headline: Turk petrochemical, oil workers to block shipments.

text.p: More than 22,000 workers at Turkey's leading state oil and petrochemical plants would obstruct shipments of goods from the factories for two days, a trade union spokesman said on Wednesday.

"We will not allow products tomorrow and on Friday to be transported from the factories to the industries which use them as raw or semi-finished materials, to force the employer to an agreement in ongoing pay talks," Ali Bugdayci, head of the Petrol-Is Kocaeli branch, told Reuters.

The protest will take place in Petkim Petrokimya Holding A.S., Tupras Turkiye Petrol Rafinerileri A.S., Turkiye Petrolleri Anonim Ortakligi (TPAO), Petrol Ofisi A.S., Botas Boru Tasimaciligi A.S. plants which are mainly located in the western and southern coastal regions.

Petrol-Is officials urged the government to take steps towards an accord to end three-month-long collective bargaining talks between the cabinet and trade union confederation Turk-Is representing more than 500,000 public workers.

"The government must stop resisting our demands and sign an accord before the Bayram (religious holiday between April 17-21) or else our actions will continue," Bayram Yildirim, president of Petrol-Is, said in a statement on Wednesday.
The negotiations between Turk-Is, the biggest confederation in Turkey, and the government are for a two-year contract beginning from January 1.

Petrol-Is, which operates in major oil related industries, and Hava-Is, active in the aviation industry led by national carrier Turk Hava Yollari, also want to sign separate labour contracts with the government because of the special characteristics of their sectors, Bugdayci said.
